hero.purpose: The Landing claim only. Two lines maximum, balanced, condensed on the width axis.

headline.purpose: Section titles inside .rule-head, always followed by a hairline that runs to the frame edge.

title.purpose: Pipeline step names and module-level headings set in prose.

body.purpose: Ledes and paragraphs. Measure held to 46-68ch.

readout.purpose: Field labels, module heads, stage rails, head readouts. Mono with tabular figures, always.

slug.purpose: The transmission rail at the top of every page: date, mode, dimensions, sample rate.

lcd.purpose: Inside the console's 160x144 canvas only. 5x7 cells, 6px advance, 26 characters per line.

shadows.name: lift-1
shadows.purpose: Small lifted objects at rest, such as file cards.

shadows.name: inset-well
shadows.purpose: Every recessed surface: inputs, drop targets, switch tracks, canvas stages.

shadows.name: button-extrusion
shadows.purpose: Primary controls. The solid plate is the button's thickness; press travels 3px.

shadows.name: button-extrusion-pressed
shadows.purpose: The bottomed-out state paired with translateY(3px).

shadows.name: shell-extrusion
shadows.purpose: The console only. Two solid plates give the case its side wall; two soft casts put it on the desk.

shadows.name: screen-well
shadows.purpose: The LCD set into its bezel as a well, not a rectangle.

shadows.name: screen-glow
shadows.purpose: Added to the screen well only when the console is powered on.

shadows.name: focus-ring-lcd
shadows.purpose: Input focus: the stroke shifts to screen shade and a translucent LCD ring appears outside.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions on controls (0.09-0.2s).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Arrivals and reveals: the console's entrance, the nav underline, the paint-down.

motion.name: console-arrive
motion.value: console-arrive 0.85s var(--ease-out) both — from opacity 0 / translateY(22px) rotate(-3.4deg) to none
motion.purpose: The only entrance animation in the system. Landing's console settling onto the desk.

motion.name: paint-down
motion.value: paint-down 1.05s var(--ease-out) both — clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0 0 0 0)
motion.purpose: Receive's rebuilt picture resolving one slice at a time, the way the decoder works.

motion.name: paint-line
motion.value: paint-line 1.05s var(--ease-out) both — top 0 to 100%, fading at the end
motion.purpose: The bright LCD-highlight line leading the paint-down reveal.

motion.name: scope-sweep
motion.purpose: The idle scope reading as a powered panel waiting for a file, not a blank card.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) — all animation/transition durations 0.01ms; .scope-empty::after and .recovered-frame::after removed outright
motion.purpose: Motion is removed, not merely shortened.

components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-stagerail { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; margin: 0; padding: 14px 0; list-style: none; border-top: 1px solid #223129; border-bottom: 1px solid #223129; } .ds-stagerail li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding-right: 22px; margin-right: 22px; font-family: 'Spline Sans Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.07em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #869A82; border-right: 1px solid #223129; } .ds-stagerail li:last-child { border-right: 0; margin-right: 0; padding-right: 0; } .ds-stagerail li.is-done { color: #A9B8A4; } .ds-stagerail li.is-now { color: #A8B78A; } .ds-led { display: inline-block; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: #2A3A2C; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.6); } .ds-led-done { background: #4E6144; box-shadow: none; } .ds-led-open { background: #A8B78A; box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(168,183,138,0.75), inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.4); } .ds-led-locked { background: #A63B46; box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(166,59,70,0.8), inset 0 1px 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.3); }

narrative.overview:
A wirephoto press-transmission desk in a dark green room, lit from one side, with a bone-ivory handheld console sitting on it. Everything that is not the console is the room: recessed panels, hairline rules, tabular figures, silkscreen labels. The console's four-tone olive screen is the brightest surface on the site, and every other element is calibrated so it stays that way. The world is physical rather than graphic — things are wells cut into panels, plates extruded from a single upper-left light, and buttons that actually travel down when pressed.

The register is instrumentation, not consumer software. Every number is a measurement and is set in tabular mono; every heading is condensed news type; every state is said by a lit dot rather than a coloured pill. Density is high on the operating surfaces (Send, Receive) and asymmetric on Landing, where the claim reads down the left and the object sits over the right edge of the log the way a device sits on paper.

The world declines the category's default arrangement: no centred gradient headline, no animated neon waveform hero, no glass feature cards. It equally declines the warm-cream-and-serif opposite. Ground is dark green, and it stays dark.
keyCharacteristics: One light source, upper left, and all depth obeys it
Oxide red exclusively on pressable things
Every readout in tabular mono; every measurement right-aligned
A four-tone LCD ramp treated as a closed material
Hairline rules and dispatch slugs instead of cards and containers
Wells are recessed, panels are lifted, and borders never fake either

rules.name: The Pressable Red Rule
rules.body: Oxide is worn only by things that can be pressed. A disabled primary control gives the colour back — it becomes a raised neutral plate with a hairline inset — rather than staying red and dimming.

rules.name: The Closed Ramp Rule
rules.body: Inside the LCD panel, only the four ramp tones exist. No fifth tone, no antialiased intermediate, no webfont. Everything drawn there is drawn at 160x144 and rendered image-rendering: pixelated.

rules.name: The Colour-Means-State Rule
rules.body: Colour states are inherited and fixed: signal is #7F9166, open/recovered is #A8B78A, locked/peak/alert is #8C2F39. Learned once, they hold on the log, the file cards, the stage rails and the console's battery lamp.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a number, a filename, a rate, a dimension or a code is set in Spline Sans Mono with tabular figures and right-aligned in its column. Anything that is a sentence is set in Archivo.

rules.name: The Three Registers Rule
rules.body: Each face has one territory and never crosses: Archivo for display and UI, Spline Sans Mono for readouts, the bitmap face inside the LCD canvas. The site footer's slogan is prose and therefore gives the mono face back.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Display type is condensed on the variable axis ('wdth' 84-92), never faked with transform: scaleX() or a separate condensed family. Body sits at 100.

rules.name: The Rail Rule
rules.body: The dispatch slug and the head readout both depend on a left run and a right anchor. When the row wraps, the anchor takes its own line rather than colliding with the tail of the run.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Every shadow falls down and to the right of a single upper-left source. No element carries a shadow that contradicts it, and no element uses a border to imply a raise.

rules.name: The Real Travel Rule
rules.body: A pressed control moves. The press state translates by the exact height of its extrusion plate and replaces the outer stack with an inset one, so the button appears to bottom out.

rules.name: The Singular Corner Rule
rules.body: The swept 94px corner belongs to the console. Nothing else in the system may borrow it.

dos: Do put every number, filename, rate and dimension in Spline Sans Mono with tabular figures, right-aligned in its column.
Do condense display type on Archivo's variable width axis ('wdth' 84-92) and leave body at 100.
Do build depth from a stacked shadow consistent with one upper-left light: an inset highlight on the lit edge, an inset shade on the shadowed one, and a soft cast below.
Do recess anything a user types or draws into (well tone plus Inset Well) and lift anything that groups content (panel tone plus Lift 2).
Do say state with the .led dot and the inherited state colours — signal, open, locked — everywhere state appears.
Do make a press physically travel: translate by the plate height and swap to an inset stack.
Do open every page with the dispatch slug on its hairline, carrying real transmission data.
Do keep the LCD canvas to its four tones and its bitmap face, rendered pixelated at 160x144.
Do give an outline back on focus — 2px solid #A8B78A at 3px offset — on every interactive element.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: the sweep and the paint-line are removed outright, not merely shortened.
donts: Don't use oxide red on anything that cannot be pressed — not a heading, a rule, a border, a badge, or an icon that is not a control.
Don't keep a disabled control red. It gives the colour back.
Don't use a border to imply elevation. Strokes are inset 0 0 0 1px; lift comes from shadow.
Don't ship a solid zero-blur offset shadow on its own. A hard plate is the body of an extrusion and must sit in a stack with a soft cast; a bare block shadow is not this world's device.
Don't introduce a fifth tone, an antialiased webfont, or a high-resolution graphic inside the LCD panel.
Don't reuse the 23px 23px 94px 23px swept corner on anything but the console.
Don't set a measurement in Archivo or a sentence in the mono face.

Don't add scroll-triggered fade-ups. Entrance motion is limited to the console's arrival on Landing; after that, motion answers an action — Receive's paint-down reveal with its leading line, and the idle scope's sweep.
Don't animate width, height or layout properties for state feedback; use transform and opacity (the nav underline scales, it does not grow).
Don't let expression obscure task, state or affordance on Send and Receive — the module language carries the world there, not decoration.
Don't change the import order on Receive: Simulate.css first, then Receive.css. .module, .drop, .filecard, .lockfields and .switch are defined in the former and shared.
